newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Spring/White Wheat-Spring bids mostly higher.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Spring/White Wheat-Spring bids mostly higher.

text.p: Spring wheat basis values were mostly higher on Friday in sympathy with gains in MGE futures and supported by continued slow farmer sales in parts of the Northern Plains, dealers said.
MGE May futures ended up 5-1/4 cents at $4.02-3/4 a bushel.

One supportive facter was a bullishly construed estimate of 1997 U.S. spring wheat acreage. Traders said Memphis-based analytical firm Sparks Companies Friday pegged 1997 U.S. spring wheat acreage at 18.59 million acres, below the previous outlook for 20.312 million.
There were also concerns about weather problems in the U.S. spring wheat region of the upper Midwest which snagged movement.
"Snow is causing transportation problems," a Minnesota dealer said.

Frigid weather was forecast this weekend for the central and southern Plains, but meteorologists doubt the cold will be a threat to the hard red winter wheat crop. Forecasts call for single-digit Fahrenheit temperatures late Friday and Saturday across Nebraska, Iowa and northern Kansas. Single-digit to mid-teens were likely from central Kansas to northern Oklahoma.
